gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 diagnoses incorrect EAKF transform normalization and a missing matrix factor in a covariance-matching formula. It does not recognise the distinct failure that finite second moments do not support a universal root-N empirical-covariance rate, nor the need for finite fourth-moment and dependence assumptions.

ISSUE-003 identifies the same ETKF transform covariance mismatch: omitting the factor (N-1)^(-1) makes the anomaly covariance correction too large, violating the required Gaussian-consistent covariance condition. It also explicitly recognises the resulting possible indefiniteness and supplies the corrected formula and square-root construction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed ETKF condition for T T^T is missing the (N-1)^(-1) normalization, so the induced analysis covariance has an over-scaled decrement instead of the stipulated Kalman covariance; the right-hand side can consequently be indefinite and lack the claimed principal square root.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated ETKF transform produces an analysis covariance with the correction term too large by a factor of N-1, rather than the required covariance.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction derives the same covariance discrepancy, identifies the missing (N-1)^(-1) factor, and gives the corrected transform equation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The erroneous right-hand side may be indefinite, so the stipulated principal symmetric square root need not exist and the construction is undefined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly shows possible indefiniteness, states that the principal square root may not exist, and links this to the same corrected normalization.
